item.title: Slice puts its MGA inside brokers' ChatGPT and Claude assistants via MCP
item.description: Slice Insurance Technologies, an AI-enabled MGA, has put its Model Context Protocol (MCP) server into live production, so selected agents, brokers and wholesalers can work with Slice directly from assistants such as ChatGPT and Claude instead of switching platforms. Slice Mind orchestrates tasks, the newly live RiskDNA supplies structured risk data, and Insurance Cloud Services carries out supported transactions while keeping policy records current. Access is limited to chosen partners, and every transaction still depends on underwriting rules, carrier authority and required sign-offs.

item.title: Aurora lands IA Capital backing to take its QBE-proven algorithmic underwriting to more carriers
item.description: Aurora, the MGA behind QBE's British Marine Yacht P&I product, secured investment from New York-based IA Capital Group to offer its white-labelled algorithmic underwriting-as-a-service model to other insurers writing complex and specialty lines; terms were not disclosed. On the QBE product, brokers can move from quote to bind in under 10 minutes, down from days, with AI ingesting unstructured email submissions while each product applies the carrier's own appetite, pricing and brand under delegated authority. Aurora says the funding will pay for re-platforming as AI-native and scaling across more products and insurers.

item.title: Montréal's Eight by Zero raises $3M seed with Canada Life as strategic investor
item.description: Eight by Zero (8/0), a Montréal-based interoperability platform for insurance, closed a $3M USD seed round led by Diagram, with Canada Life participating as a strategic investor and Munich Re Life US working with it on employee data connectivity for group and disability clients. The platform replaces hand-built, point-to-point employer integrations with a single connectivity layer, so carriers get current employee data on leaves, injuries, hour changes and departures for each line they write. Already in use with multiple carriers across North America, 8/0 will use the funds for product development, new lines of coverage and implementation capacity.

item.title: Minnesota issues AI bulletin spelling out governance expectations for insurers
item.description: The Minnesota Department of Commerce issued Administrative Bulletin 2026-4, reminding all licensed insurers that decisions made or supported by AI systems must comply with insurance laws, including unfair trade practice and unfair discrimination rules. The department encourages insurers to maintain a written AI Systems (AIS) Program with controls scaled to the risk of adverse consumer outcomes, including testing for errors and bias and accounting for reliance on third-party data and models. It also sets out the kind of information and documentation the department may request when investigating or examining an insurer's AI use.

item.title: Alpine Specialty launches as an AI-assisted E&S casualty MGA with $3M
item.description: Raleigh-based Alpine Specialty launched as an MGA focused on small-account excess and surplus casualty, closing $3 million in initial financing led by Will Thorndike and naming James River veteran Allen Clyborne chief underwriting officer. Its proprietary Summit software uses agentic AI to collect and organize risk information, apply underwriting guidelines and prepare multiple coverage options, while human underwriters keep risk selection, pricing and binding decisions. Alpine will start with contractors' liability and plans to begin binding through appointed wholesale brokers in summer 2027.

item.title: Gradient AI launches Sentinel to flag high-cost group health conditions from lab data
item.description: Gradient AI launched Sentinel, an add-on to its SAIL group health underwriting and stop-loss platform that mines lab results to surface potentially high-cost conditions before they appear on medical or pharmacy claims. Because it uses the same census data SAIL already relies on, underwriters get earlier lab-based signals layered onto existing claims insights without onboarding a new system. Gradient AI says the payoff is more accurate rate-setting and better Medical Loss Ratio performance for group health and stop-loss writers.

item.title: Hodinkee and Zillion embed a new watch and jewelry insurance program in Hodinkee's app
item.description: Hodinkee, whose insurance business covers more than $1 billion in insured assets, partnered with embedded insurance provider Zillion, whose product is backed by Tokio Marine and AXA XL, on a new watch and jewelry protection program that launched November 16. The program embeds Zillion's coverage, exclusive savings and concierge claims in Hodinkee's mobile app for Hodinkee Community members and existing policyholders. It is available across the US, with Washington State coverage anticipated in early 2027.

item.title: AI Tool: Gemini Notebook: turn your sources into interactive sites
item.description: Google's Gemini Notebook can now turn the sources in a notebook into interactive sites: type "make me a site" in the notebook chat with a description, such as an interactive dashboard to explore data or a project tracker for tasks and deadlines, then open it in a new tab or share it. The feature is rolling out globally on the web for users 18+, including Google Workspace subscribers, and is coming soon to the mobile app. Practical use: load a client's policy wordings, schedules and loss runs into a notebook and ask for a renewal tracker site that lists key dates, limits and open items to review with the client, then check it against the documents.

item.title: AI Tool: Microsoft Copilot: Home brings Chat and Cowork together
item.description: At Microsoft Ignite 2026, Microsoft made Copilot Home generally available as one starting point where Chat and Cowork come together: ask a quick question in Chat or hand off a whole workflow to Cowork, with Auto routing choosing the right models and effort for each task, and OpenAI or Anthropic models selectable under organizational policy. Microsoft says Work IQ reasons over your emails, Teams meetings and chats, and documents to find what matters for the task at hand. Practical use: ask Copilot to gather everything on a commercial renewal from email threads, Teams meeting notes and Word memos into one summary of open underwriter questions before you call the client.
